status_summary: Sunset provisions are operative for some energy regulators and no commission was found. Executive Order 14270 (signed 2025-04-09, 90 FR 15643) directs EPA, DOE, FERC, NRC and certain Interior and Army Corps components to add conditional sunset dates to covered existing regulations and to give new covered rules sunset dates no more than five years out; FERC published a direct final rule on 2025-10-21 (90 FR 48397), effective 2025-12-05, under which 53 listed regulations cease to have effect on 2026-12-05 unless extended, and the NRC published a direct final rule on 2025-12-03 (90 FR 55621) whose effective date of 2026-01-08 it confirmed on 2026-01-08 (91 FR 553), withdrawing one amendment, with listed provisions sunsetting one year after the rule took effect unless extended. Executive Orders 14192 (ten-for-one repeal) and 14219 (review of all regulations) do not provide sunsets or a commission, and no presidentially appointed Regulatory Reduction Commission or annual repeal package to Congress was found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14270 (signed 2025-04-09) on zero-based regulatory budgeting with conditional sunset dates was published.
FERC published a direct final rule (90 FR 48397), effective 2025-12-05, adding a conditional sunset date of 2026-12-05 to 53 regulations.
NRC published a direct final rule adding conditional sunset dates to listed regulations, effective 2026-01-08 unless significant adverse comments were received.
NRC confirmed the 2026-01-08 effective date of its sunset rule (91 FR 553), withdrawing the amendment that would have added a sunset date to 10 CFR 50.150 on aircraft impact assessment.

title: Ease trade adjustment with regulatory sunsets and a Regulatory Reduction Commission
uncertainties: DOE published a related zero-based regulating rule on 2026-05-29, and the EPA, Interior and Army Corps sunset rules were not checked in the Federal Register text. Whether the FERC rule took effect without significant adverse comment was not confirmed beyond a later partial rescission notice effective 2026-01-20 seen in search results. The count of 53 FERC regulations is taken from the rule's own statement and could not be reproduced exactly from its table of contents. A further NRC notice of 2026-02-03 (FR Doc. 2026-02165), described as a confirmation with a correction, was not read. Executive Orders 14192 and 14219 are context for deregulation, and the absence of a commission rests on searches and on Executive Order 14270 creating none. The match is partial because the sunsets cover regulations of named energy agencies, not new regulations generally, and are not framed as trade adjustment measures.
